newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer expects complaints on hip joints.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer expects complaints on hip joints.

text.p: Swiss engineering concern Sulzer AG said it expected complaints to be filed against it arising from patients who received its titaniam stems for cemented hip joint replacements.

Sulzer, in a statement, said that talks between the firm, its liability insurer and the attorney representing the Swiss magazine "Beobachter" had broken down. About one year ago, the magazine had called for patients with the hip joint replacements to report problems, Sulzer said.
"Under such premises, a complaint is likely to be brought against Sulzer. Sulzer regrets these developments," Sulzer said.

The company said it had thoroughly evaluated the complaints. "After a year of most intensive investigations, there is no reliable scientific data showing that Sulzer's cemented titanium stems for hip joints had a higher rate of loosening compared with cemented stems made of other materials," Sulzer said.

"With every kind of implanted hip joint, there is a chance that sooner or later signs of loosening will occur," Sulzer said. It said that age and sex of the patient could pay a role, as well as factors like choice and style of the implant, the type of operation, the medical history of the patient and the patient's lifestyle.
